label: copy-phase input w, late in the sequence
explanation: Fires almost only when the fed-back input token is w during the copy phase: 99.9% of activations and essentially all activation mass. It is a late-sequence w detector. The firing rate and magnitude climb steeply with absolute step t (rate on copy-phase w is near 0 for t<=11 and about 2.5% of all steps by t=15-17), so most mass comes from L=8-9 sequences at recall_idx 5-8. The strongest activations come from w input at the last or second-to-last copy step, often in sequences ending with a repeated w w. It never fires on w in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other token. Restricting to t>=14 gives dev F1 0.69 (P 0.65, R 0.75, mass recall 0.85). Copy-phase w at moderate t (12-13) gives weak activations that are missed. Many late w steps (t=14, recall_idx 4-5) stay inactive, so the threshold in t is soft and precision is incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: w, -, <DEL>, o, g, u; least: h, q, 1, v) and the token being output (most: w, d, l, s, o, m; least: h, j, 1, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=7, t=15, t=17.
